PullRequest.Title: eslint: flag disposables registered after await without a disposal check
PullRequest.Body:
Adds the lint rule `local/code-no-register-after-await`. It reports a disposable registered on `this` after an `await` when nothing in between re-checks whether the object was disposed or the operation cancelled:

- `this._register(x)`
- `this.<store>.add(x)`
- `this.<mutable>.value = x`
- `this.<map>.set(k, x)`

Adding to a disposed `DisposableStore` only warns and leaks the value, and a disposed `MutableDisposable` silently drops it. The leak then usually fails the leak check of an unrelated later test.

To make the fix a one-liner, this also adds `Disposable._registerOrDispose(x)` and `DisposableStore.addOrDispose(x)`. They dispose `x` instead of registering it when the owner is already disposed. The rule's message points to them:

```ts
this._registerOrDispose(await this.doCreate());
```

The rule is syntactic and per function. It follows branches, loops, `switch` and `try`/`catch`/`finally`. A condition on `isDisposed`/`disposed`, `isCancellationRequested` or `aborted` counts as a check, and so do `throwIfAborted()`-style calls. An awaited `raceCancellationError(...)` does not count, because it can resolve after the token was cancelled. Details are in `.eslint-plugin-local/README.md`.

The 178 files that already report the rule are listed in `.eslint-allowed-register-after-await-files`.

This PR was split up. Follow-ups based on this branch:
- #346296: `interruptAtEveryStep` test helper and leak fixes
- #346297: chat editing session leak, and release of its barriers on disposal

Originally by @alexdima.

**Validation**
- `node --test .eslint-plugin-local/tests/code-no-register-after-await.test.ts`: 51 passing
- `scripts/test.bat --run src/vs/base/test/common/lifecycle.test.ts`: 32 passing
- `pnpm run eslint` on the changed files: clean
- A full-repo scan of the rule outside the baseline: no reports

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The scope transition and CI call path are explicit, as is the planned repeated trigger for baseline removals. Exact elapsed time depends on cache warmth and repository size, but the repository-wide file discovery/hash cardinality versus one changed source file is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem reads/content hashing and, on cold cache entries, parsing plus AST analysis for every JavaScript/TypeScript file in the repository
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Each edit to the 211-line migration allowlist expands from the one fixed source file to every path matched by eslintFilter; cost grows with total repository JS/TS files rather than the number of files removed from the allowlist.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Incremental cleanup PRs incur full-repository ESLint I/O and CPU, increasing the Hygiene & ESLint job latency from the intended changed-file check to a repository-wide check.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this entry, fixing one source file used getEslintScope's changed-files branch and linted that file only; this allowlist did not force a full lint.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added path matches eslintFullCheckPaths, so getEslintScope returns kind 'full' whenever any entry is removed from .eslint-allowed-register-after-await-files, and build/eslint.ts expands that to the complete eslintFilter.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added RIGHT-side entry `'.eslint-allowed-register-after-await-files',` at build/lib/changedFiles.ts:37 makes matchesAny classify every modification of the new migration baseline as a full ESLint check.
Findings.Title: Scope allowlist cleanups to the affected files
Findings.Impact: The README explicitly requires removing a file from this 211-line baseline when it is fixed. Every such follow-up now sends all repository JS/TS files through lintFiles instead of the affected source file; warm cache still requires repository-wide discovery/content-cache validation, while cold or invalidated entries also parse and run the new rule.
Findings.Evidence: build/lib/changedFiles.ts:161-165 returns full scope for any matchesAny hit, and build/eslint.ts:57-63 maps full scope to getEslintFilePatterns([]), whose build/filters.ts:262-270 globs all JS/TS. The PR workflow invokes eslint --changed-since for every PR (.github/workflows/pr.yml:301-306), while the new README at line 172 directs each cleanup to edit this allowlist.
Findings.Recommendation: Special-case this migration baseline so a cleanup lints the changed source files plus any paths removed from the allowlist (derive removed entries from the diff), rather than treating every baseline edit as globally affecting all lint targets.

Scenarios.Scenario: A follow-up PR fixes one baseline violation and removes that source path from .eslint-allowed-register-after-await-files.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The PR Hygiene & ESLint step invokes `eslint --changed-since`; `getEslintScope` must select scope before ESLint can finish, and the added full-check classification makes repository-wide linting part of the blocking CI path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One synchronous git subprocess per changed-since scope calculation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one git subprocess ran before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks scope calculation, but its cardinality and placement are unchanged by this PR.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: ESLint expands the full JS/TS globs, validates content-cache entries, and reads/parses files that miss cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: All repository JS/TS lint targets after one allowlist edit, rather than the fixed source files in the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: A source-only cleanup used the changed-files scope and passed only those source paths to lintFiles.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All discovery/cache validation and misses must complete before the CI lint step succeeds.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total lintable repository JS/TS files, triggered by removing any of the 211 baseline entries; effective cardinality is the full eslintFilter even when only one violation is fixed.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: ESLint uses `concurrency: 'auto'`; this parallelizes file processing but does not reduce aggregate repository-wide discovery, hashing, parsing, or rule work.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: On a cold cache, every target is parsed and analyzed. On a warm content cache, unchanged targets can skip analysis, but the full glob still discovers the repository and validates cache/content state; there is no coalescing back to the affected paths.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added path is directly consumed by `matchesAny`, which returns full scope, and `getEslintRun` directly expands full scope to eslintFilter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact wall time depends on runner filesystem speed and cache reuse, but the full-repository versus one-file cardinality transition is deterministic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable boundary fan-out: each required incremental baseline cleanup now forces full-repository lint I/O and possible parsing instead of affected-file linting.

Scenarios.Scenario: A developer or CI run lints ordinary changed TypeScript/JavaScript files after the new rule is enabled.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing ESLint parsing and the new rule's per-async-function analysis complete before lint results return.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read the lint target and ESLint cache/config files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One set of reads per requested lint target plus small fixed configuration files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: ESLint already read and parsed each requested target; the new rule adds a bounded in-memory pass over async function bodies.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing blocking lint input; the diff adds only the small allowlist configuration read and in-memory AST analysis.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: AST nodes in async functions and class bodies in the lint targets; class field classification is cached per class and await detection is cached per node.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Files are processed with ESLint `concurrency: 'auto'`; analysis within one AST is synchronous and bounded, with loop fixed-point evaluation at most twice per state transition.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Content-cache hits skip lint analysis; misses run the rule. The rule retains WeakMap entries only for the lifetime of the linted AST/analyzer.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for bounded traversal and absence of external calls in the rule.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No benchmark is supplied, but implementation inspection shows linear/bounded traversal rather than unbounded history or per-node external calls.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: a bounded AST traversal is expected work for the intentionally enabled lint rule, with no proven disproportionate regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: An object is disposed while awaiting creation of a disposable, then the continuation calls addOrDispose/_registerOrDispose or thenRegisterOrDispose.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the promise resolves, the helper synchronously checks one boolean and either inserts one disposable or disposes that one value before the continuation proceeds.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One created disposable per helper invocation; no collection-wide scan or retained history is introduced.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: JavaScript continuation ordering remains serialized for the check and add/dispose operation; no new parallel resource creation is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved. A live store retains the value exactly as `add` did; a disposed store immediately releases it instead of retaining/leaking it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed lifecycle code is direct constant-time branching around the existing add/dispose operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Individual `dispose()` implementations can vary in cost, but disposal is required cleanup and occurs only when ownership has already ended.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression: the helper bounds cleanup lifetime and the thenRegisterOrDispose refactor preserves its prior branch behavior.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and all diff pages. One medium-confidence-impact, high-mechanism-confidence CI boundary-fanout finding was submitted for classifying every migration-allowlist edit as a full-repository ESLint run. The lint rule traversal and lifecycle helper changes are bounded and introduce no additional reportable performance regressions.
